The transaction inserts strategy_state_events idempotently, locks/version-updates strategy_state only for new events, records writer/run/last_event metadata, and supports expected-version conflicts. Wired live option-chain node readiness to require Postgres storage only when live entry submit is requested; it now checks required migration version, acquires and heartbeats a runtime_lease, loads storage-backed state, and passes a StrategyStatePersistenceHandle into AlpacaOptionsEntryStrategy. The strategy refuses live entries when persistence is missing/unhealthy, keeps in-memory state updates immediate, and enqueues accepted plus terminal rejected/denied state mutations through the async sink. Validated with cargo fmt -p nautilus-alpaca, cargo check -p nautilus-alpaca --features live --bins, and a disposable /tmp harness against local Alpaca Postgres that acquired a lease, enqueued duplicate entry_accepted mutations through the public persistence handle, verified one event plus snapshot version 1 and lease row, then deleted the generated smoke rows.

Postgres durability epic completed. Storage schema now uses sqlx migrations; strategy_state has version/writer/run/event metadata; strategy_state_events and runtime_lease are in Postgres; persist_strategy_state_mutation writes event plus snapshot transactionally and idempotently; the option-chain live node gates live entry submit on storage readiness, migration version, runtime lease, and persistence handle health. Validated with cargo fmt/check and local Alpaca Postgres smoke harnesses for migration application, idempotent state mutation, runtime lease acquisition, async persistence enqueue, and smoke-row cleanup.

Implemented Alpaca-owned reconciliation scoping: startup/reconnect snapshots include all open orders unbounded, bound historical orders and fills with a default 60m lookback when Nautilus does not provide one, and leave current positions unfiltered. Validation: cargo fmt -p nautilus-alpaca; cargo check -p nautilus-alpaca --features live --bins; cargo test -p nautilus-alpaca --features live --lib; bounded SPY 2026-06-30 live-node smoke with submission disabled and kill switch on showed startup reconciliation received 0 orders/fills/positions and no instrument-cache skipped-order warning; post-run operator status showed 0 open orders and 0 positions.

Implemented live-submit readiness safeguards for the Alpaca Nautilus strategy path. Live submit now requires current Postgres migrations, an acquired runtime lease, a healthy state persistence sink, startup account-admission checks, and broker/state reconciliation before the node can submit. Shared broker/state reconciliation now blocks live submit on unmanaged positions, unmanaged open orders, or partial-position state. Persistence write/queue failures and runtime lease heartbeat loss mark the persistence handle unhealthy and emit operator evidence, so later entries are denied. Graceful live-node shutdown releases the runtime lease; crash safety still falls back to TTL. Validation: cargo fmt -p nautilus-alpaca; cargo check -p nautilus-alpaca --features live --bins; cargo test -p nautilus-alpaca --features live --lib; bounded live-submit-gated smoke with ALPACA_SUBMIT=true, ALPACA_OPTIONS_LIVE_ENTRY_SUBMIT_ENABLED=true, ALPACA_KILL_SWITCH=true acquired lease, emitted live_submit_readiness with storage_ready/lease_held/broker_state_reconciled, startup reconciliation saw 0 orders/fills/positions, exited cleanly, and emitted runtime_lease_released. Post-run operator status showed account ACTIVE, 0 open orders, 0 positions, storage migrations applied, and engine blocked by kill switch/submission-disabled container gates.

Implemented and proved AlpacaOptionsEntryStrategy admission parity against the legacy account-engine path. Shared admission now carries account-tradability reasons into the Nautilus strategy, applies the same persisted StrategyState/fleet/risk/daily limits, classifies candidate-leg and same-underlying broker conflicts from the Nautilus cache, counts open broker order intents for max-open-orders admission, and emits structured entry_decision evidence for dry-run and selected_but_blocked outcomes. Fixed option-chain trade-date derivation so daily risk state uses the configured market trade-date clock instead of stale quote slice timestamps; scan events now include trade_date. Live evidence: account engine dry-run and Nautilus strategy dry-run both selected SPY call_credit legs SPY260706C00743000/SPY260706C00745000 with reason submission_disabled; account engine selected-but-blocked and Nautilus strategy selected-but-blocked both selected the same legs and blocked with risk_max_open_orders current=0 limit=0. Live-submit-gated Nautilus proof acquired readiness/lease, startup reconciliation saw 0 orders/fills/positions, emitted live_submit_readiness, emitted selected_but_blocked, released the runtime lease, and post-run operator status showed account ACTIVE, 0 open orders, 0 positions, storage migrations current. Validation: cargo fmt -p nautilus-alpaca; cargo check -p nautilus-alpaca --features live --bins; cargo test -p nautilus-alpaca --features live --lib; git diff --check.

Readiness and admission parity prerequisites are complete; nt-9l3.8 carries the remaining market-hours validation acceptance so the legacy-entry-loop removal work can proceed without falsely claiming a market-hours submit occurred on Saturday.

Removed the legacy Alpaca account-engine entry loop. alpaca-options-engine is now management-only for existing entries; direct entry scan/decision/submission code and entry-only helper events were deleted from options_engine.rs/options_engine/events.rs, ALPACA_OPTIONS_LIVE_ENTRY_SUBMIT_ENABLED and node_entry_submit_enabled were removed, and the option-chain live node now uses the normal ALPACA_SUBMIT runtime gate for Nautilus strategy submission readiness. Updated active Alpaca code comments/status naming away from account-engine entry ownership. Post-run alpaca-operator-status showed account ACTIVE, trading_blocked=false, 0 open orders, 0 positions, storage migrations current, and service inactive. Actual market-hours submit validation remains tracked by nt-9l3.8.

Implemented bounded async candidate-ledger persistence for the Nautilus Alpaca live path. Option-chain scanner evidence now flows through CandidateLedgerPersistenceHandle as scanner_result and ranked candidate records; AlpacaOptionsEntryStrategy writes selected_candidate alerts for dry-run, blocked, skipped, and submitted decisions plus candidate_submit_rejected alerts for terminal reject/deny evidence. Live submit now fails closed when candidate-ledger persistence is absent or unhealthy, and runtime lease loss marks both state and candidate-ledger sinks unhealthy. The live node flushes candidate-ledger evidence before releasing the runtime lease. alpaca-operator-status now reads recent durable candidate-ledger records so last_scan and last_decision do not depend on stdout log capture. Duplicate selected-candidate alerts are suppressed per run while scanner/candidate records remain per scan. Validation: cargo fmt -p nautilus-alpaca; cargo check -p nautilus-alpaca --features live --bins; cargo test -p nautilus-alpaca --features live --lib; git diff --check; bounded live-node smoke with ALPACA_SUBMIT=true and ALPACA_MAX_OPEN_ORDERS=0 acquired readiness/lease, scanned SPY 2026-07-06, selected a call_credit candidate, blocked with risk_max_open_orders, flushed evidence, released the lease, and left the broker flat. alpaca-operator-status showed account ACTIVE, 0 open orders, 0 positions, storage migrations current, durable last_scan=scanner_result source=option_chain, and durable last_decision=selected_candidate action=selected_but_blocked reason=risk_max_open_orders. alpaca-candidate-alerts --dry-run with a 1-minute lookback showed exactly one eligible selected-candidate alert for the fresh run.
